ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Fannie Lou Hamer — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Four-month review: A1c, urine albumin, kidney function, mood, social needs, and the metformin dose

text.paragraph: Four-month review: A1c, urine albumin, kidney function, mood, social needs, and the metformin dose. [S]

Mrs. Hamer returns two months after her last review, brought by the health center's van as booked. Her home readings averaged 131/82 at the four-week phone check and 127/79 since, so no dose change was needed. She has had no low blood sugar, dizziness, cough or genital itching. She has finished the diabetes classes. The energy assistance was approved, and with SNAP and the produce program the food lasts through the month. She walks most days, though her legs ache. Her mood is steady. [S]

list.item:
Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). A1c 7.3%, from 8.6%; no low blood sugar. Just above goal. [S]
Increase metformin extended-release to three tablets (1,500 mg) with the evening meal.
A1c again in three months.

Chronic kidney disease G2 A2 (N18.2). Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 52 mg/g, down from 96; potassium 4.6 mmol/L; creatinine 1.02 mg/dL, eGFR 67: stable. [S]
Continue benazepril and dapagliflozin.
Urine albumin again in three months.

Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). At goal at home and in the clinic. [S]
Continue amlodipine-benazepril; home readings twice a week.

Transportation insecurity (Z59.82). Van rides booked for every visit since the missed check; other trips still uncertain. AHC screen now positive for transportation only. [S]
Keep rides booked at each visit; phone visits when travel is not possible.
